data.name: Greenland
data.summary: Greenland taxes residents on worldwide income at a single combined rate set by municipality (42% in Nuuk/Sermersooq, 44% in some other municipalities). As a main rule, capital gains on shares are not taxable for individuals; dividends and interest are ordinary income at the full rate, with a credit for foreign tax. Inheritances are not taxed and gifts from parents to children are tax-free. No wealth tax, no tax on private-use property and no VAT.

regimes.name: Full tax liability
regimes.description: Worldwide income taxed at a flat combined municipal + national rate (42%-44%); share gains untaxed; no inheritance, gift-to-children or wealth tax.
regimes.eligibility: Full tax liability on taking up residence (acquiring a home) or staying more than six consecutive months (PwC Residence).

capital_gains.summary: As a main rule capital gains are not taxable for individuals. Exceptions: financial contracts (derivatives) and debentures with nominal interest below 2% a year, taxed as ordinary income (42%-44%). Gains on Greenland real estate are not taxed for private individuals as a rule (PwC lists sale of Greenland real estate under limited liability income; treatment for residents not confirmed).

capital_gains.rate_basis: PwC Income determination: capital gains not taxable for individuals, except derivatives and low-coupon debentures.
capital_gains.professional_trader: Business income (individual traders) is taxed at the ordinary rates.

dividends.summary: Dividends are ordinary taxable income at the combined rate for the municipality: 42% in Kommuneqarfik Sermersooq (Nuuk) per PwC's municipal table (2020 percentages, the latest published there). Foreign income taxes are credited up to the Greenland tax on that income.
dividends.regional_differences: 44% in Kujalleq, Qeqertalik and Avannaata; 36% outside municipalities.

open_questions: 2026 municipal rates not found; PwC's 2020 table used (42% Sermersooq); a 2025 AKA withholding form reportedly also shows 42% but could not be opened. The 2024 reform raised the personal allowance and labour-market levy but kept the landsskat.
dividends.rate_basis: Sermersooq combined rate 42% (26% municipal + 10% national + 6% joint municipal, PwC table).
dividends.withholding_outbound: Dividend WHT 36%-44% by municipality (24% under chapter 3b); treaty rates for Denmark, Faroes, Iceland, Norway.
dividends.treaty_network: Full treaties only with Denmark, Faroe Islands, Iceland and Norway (plus employee-tax treaties with Guernsey, Isle of Man, Jersey). No treaty relief for US or most EU source dividends.

sources.title: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries: Greenland - Individual - Other taxes

wealth_tax.property_tax_note: No tax on property for private use; 1.5% stamp duty on real estate deeds.

inheritance.summary: Inheritance is generally not taxable. Gifts are taxable income, except gifts to a spouse, children, stepchildren and their descendants, parents and grandparents, which are exempt.

sources.title: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries: Greenland - Individual - Other taxes

inheritance.gift_tax: Gifts to children exempt; other gifts taxed as income at 42%-44%.

residency.tax_residency_test: Full liability on taking up residence (acquiring a home) or after six consecutive months' stay (PwC Residence).

routes.name: Danish and Nordic citizens
routes.requirements: Danish citizens may live in Greenland freely; Nordic citizens have facilitated rights. EU free movement does not extend to Greenland (not an EU territory).

routes.name: Others
routes.requirements: Residence and work permits under Danish/Greenlandic immigration rules; no passive-income or investor route found.

sources.title: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries: Greenland - Individual - Residence

corporate.summary: 25% corporate tax (26.5% if the on-account payment is not made); dividends paid are deductible; dividend WHT 36%-44%.

data.us_citizen_notes: No US-Greenland treaty; US citizens remain subject to US federal tax. US source dividends suffer US WHT without treaty reduction for non-US residents.
open_questions: A Siumut motion for a 30% flat tax (2026) is only a proposal.

succession.name: Greenland (Denmark)
succession.summary: Greenland still applies the old Danish Inheritance Act of 1964, not the 2008 Danish act. I could not read its text, so the size of the protected share is not confirmed. Denmark is not in the Hague Trusts Convention, and I found no trust or private foundation law for Greenland.
succession.reserved_share: Children and spouse have compulsory shares (tvangsarv) under the Danish tradition and the 1964 Greenland act; amounts and the article were not verified.
succession.foreign_law_note: Not sourced. The Greenland act's conflict rules and Danish rules on foreign law were not read.
succession.trust_note: Denmark is not listed in the HCCH table, and the Convention has not been extended to Greenland. No trust statute was found. Foundations (fonde) exist in Danish-based law; whether Greenland has its own foundation law that allows a family foundation was not checked.
open_questions: Inheritance Act for Greenland (Act 154 of 27 May 1964): the compulsory shares and article numbers were not read; forced_heirship 'yes' rests on the general Danish model and should be verified.

A 2017 parliamentary question said Greenland still used the old act and that the 2008 Danish act could be extended by royal decree; a 2022 Naalakkersuisut proposal on modernising inheritance law exists. The outcome is unknown; check for a new Greenland inheritance act.
Foundation (fond) and trust rules for Greenland were not sourced.
Trust/foundation availability marked unclear: no statute was found, which does not show that none exists.
